summary.headline: Navneet Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 31% to INR324 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 150% to INR20 crore, with margin at 6.2%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 31-32% YoY from INR246 crore to INR324 crore, and standalone EBITDA rose 150% to INR20 crore (margin 3.3% to 6.2%). Standalone PAT was INR6 crore versus a loss of INR6 crore a year earlier. Publication revenue rose about 53.8% to INR140 crore, partly on Q1 spillover, while domestic and export stationery margins were pressured by brand spending, manpower, a GST reversal, new plant depreciation and export discounts given under US tariffs. Management guided to better H2 profitability and said the K12 Techno stake sale proceeds (INR330 crore received, up to INR70 crore more pending) are to be deployed after a board decision.

segments.name: Publication
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR140 crore, up c.53.8% YoY with Q1 spillover; H1 revenue INR544 crore, up 6.7%. Curriculum change cycle runs FY26 to two more years, moving to higher grades.

segments.name: Domestic stationery
segments.commentary: Revenue INR52 crore, up c.34%. Margins fell on branding spend, senior manpower for non-paper categories and a one-time GST reversal on inventory; about 70 new items launched in the last six months.

segments.name: Export stationery
segments.commentary: Revenue INR132 crore. Margins hit by first-ever discounts given on agreed prices due to US tariffs, reversed around June-July; management says discounts have now been discontinued.

segments.name: Indiannica (K12 central curriculum)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR1 crore and loss about INR9.5 crore, with returns adjustment. Management plans to merge it into Navneet, citing INR5-6 crore annual savings.

guidance_outlook: Publication growth of at least 15% expected next year, as Maharashtra grades 7, 9 and 11 and four Gujarat grades change.
FY27 export stationery revenue about INR250 crore and domestic stationery about INR200 crore for the rest of the year (rough figures).
FY27 full-year stationery margin expected about 2% lower than last year, as export revenue is concentrated in H1.
Domestic stationery growth of around 15-20% expected next year.
Export margins expected to improve from H2 FY27 as discounts have stopped.
Publication delay cost about INR20-30 crore of business in FY27 that management expects to recover next year.
capex_capacity: New plastic products plant commissioned; its depreciation and fixed costs weighed on stationery margins, and customer orders were delayed by raw material price spikes.
Common facilities serve both stationery plants, so segment-wise margins for domestic and export are not separately derived.
Government textbook delays (sold only one month after state release) pushed back school orders; management says about INR20-30 crore business shifts to next year.
Grades 3, 4 and 6 changed this year; grades 7 to 12 remain to change over the next two years.
demand_pricing: US retail offtake from shelves fell due to inflation; management says new orders are being finalised from October-November after showcasing new categories.
The 10% US tariff applies to all countries; management sees no further tariff uncertainty after the August decision not to levy the additional measures.
Paper prices rose about INR2,000 per tonne (about 3%) in the last month; mills talk of 5-10% more over the next year, which management plans to cushion in product prices.
Heavy paper buying is expected from November to April.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management more confident on exports now, and why did Q2 profitability stay weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new categories shown to US customers with orders finalising from October, the August tariff relief and a stable 10% baseline tariff. Margin pressure was attributed to one-time export discount reversals, brand and manpower spend in domestic stationery, and the new plastics plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR100 crore the breakeven for publication, and what drove the quarterly profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly profit should not be read in isolation given seasonality. For a full year, INR100 crore revenue is roughly breakeven on a 30-35% EBITDA margin, but fixed costs rise each year.

qa_highlights.question: Will Indiannica be exited?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management plans to merge Indiannica into Navneet to remove intra-group costs and indirect taxes, saving about INR5-6 crore a year, and sees central curriculum K12 as strategic, with guide-type products planned.

qa_highlights.question: How will the K12 Techno sale proceeds be used, and what stake remains?
qa_highlights.answer: INR330 crore is received, with up to INR70 crore more due in 15-20 days. Special dividend is part of the plan, with buyback and other options under board discussion; clarity is expected next quarter. About 8% stake remains after both transactions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the publication impact of delayed government textbooks?
qa_highlights.answer: The one-month post-release sales restriction and late state textbook releases (grades 3, 4 and 6 changed this year) led some schools to defer purchases, costing about INR20-30 crore that management expects back next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 stationery margin and growth expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year stationery margin expected about 2% lower than last year. FY27 revenue rough estimate is INR250 crore export and INR200 crore domestic for the rest of the year; domestic growth of 15-20% expected next year.

risks_watch: Export margin recovery in H2 depends on discounts staying discontinued and on the US retail inventory correction ending.
Paper prices could rise 5-10% over the next year, with heavy buying from November to April.
Domestic stationery margins are under pressure from sustained branding spend and new non-paper hires; management says it will spend more on brand for at least two years.
Indiannica continues to lose money in Q1-Q3; the merger savings (INR5-6 crore a year) are an estimate.
Use of K12 proceeds (special dividend, buyback or acquisition) and timing to be decided by the board, expected next quarter.
Dependence on state government textbook release timing for publication sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the publication cycle and export recovery, but defensive on quarterly profitability: management repeatedly asked analysts not to read quarterly margins and attributed weak stationery margins to one-time and deliberate investment factors. It was vague on the use of K12 proceeds, deferring details to the board.
key_quotes: So investment in branding and manpower cost overpowered the margins earned in domestic stationery, leading to drop in profitability.
So please don't ever get into quarter numbers with respect to profitability.
So with these grades changing, minimum 15% growth we are expecting.
